our_title: Core number -1 (documented 'not bound') now pins the thread to CPU 0, even outside the mask
ran: repro/COR-24/core under 'taskset -c 2-3', pristine 7.0.18: coretab {-1 -1 -1 -1} -> all four threads Cpus_allowed_list 0; {-1 3 -1 2} -> 0 3 0 2; {-5 1 -2 0} -> 0 3 2 2. 7.0.17 left -1 entries unbound (2-3). Patched (0003): 2-3 / 3 / 2-3 / 2 on 32- and 64-bit trees.
evidence: common_thread.c:927 'thrdnum %= corenbr;' (C remainder keeps -1) ; :930 'for (corenum = 0; thrdnum >= 0; corenum ++) {' not entered -> returns corenum = 0 ; threadCreate :878 'if ((corenum >= 0) && (corenum < CPU_SETSIZE))' then binds to CPU 0; s_l.tex:8224-8226 'A core index of $-1$ results in the thread not being bound to a specific core'.

fix_options.label: Return -1 for negative core numbers in threadProcessCoreNum() (committed)
fix_options.summary: 'if (thrdnum < 0) return (-1);' before the modulus; block comment documents the return values.
fix_options.tested: repro/COR-24 under taskset on both trees; 48/48 check runs
fix_options.maintainer_fit: Two lines in his routine; threadCreate already skips binding for corenum < 0.

upstream_fix_review.details: Introduced by 52dcf602: explicit coretab entries are now passed to threadProcessCoreNum(), which has no negative-input case.
upstream_fix_review.compared_with_ours: Our 7.0.17 0004 had the guard ('if (corelog < 0) return (-1);') and our 7.0.17 critique named this exact bug.

our_title: Thread start-up abort destroys lock features under waiting slaves, then frees their context
ran: TSan tree of pristine 7.0.18 (-O1 -g -fsanitize=thread), repro/COR-09 spawn_tsan 4 with FAIL_AT=3: 6 reports: data race common_thread.c:145 (unlocked write of thrdnbr) vs :322 (read under lock, T1 in threadWaitBarrier1); pthread_mutex_destroy/pthread_cond_destroy at :193-194 vs T1 in pthread_cond_wait (:331); 'destroy of a locked mutex'; 'unlock of an unlocked mutex' in T1; free of the ThreadContext at common_context.c:202 vs T1's read at :338. With glibc and no TSan the same path blocks forever in pthread_cond_destroy (gdb). Patched (0002): 0 reports, no hang.
location_7_0_18: src/libscotch/common_thread.c:145 (unlocked write), :186-194 (Exit3 spin and destroy), common_context.c:201-202 (context freed after failure)
evidence: common_thread.c:145 'contptr->thrdnbr = thrdnum;' (no lock); :186-190 'do { ... barrnbr = contptr->barrnbr; ... } while (barrnbr != thrdnbr);' satisfied by slaves parked in the start-up barrier; :193 'pthread_cond_destroy  (&contptr->conddat);'.

fix_options.label: Master joins the start-up barrier after a locked reduction (committed, same commit as COR-09)
fix_options.maintainer_fit: Three lines in his failure path.

upstream_fix_review.details: Introduced by 86559b85: in 7.0.17 the path spun forever without destroying or freeing anything; now it destroys cond/mutex with waiters (UB) and lets contextThreadInit2 free the ThreadContext the slaves still use. Same root cause as the remaining part of COR-09 (master not counted in the barrier it is expected to complete).
upstream_fix_review.compared_with_ours: Our 7.0.17 0002 had the master join the barrier, which avoids the conflation of barrier arrivals and termination acknowledgements.
